summary.headline: Zen Technologies Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs.345.1 crore (+98.8% YoY) with 38.2% operational EBITDA margin; order book rose to Rs.1,375.7 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at Rs.345.1 crore, more than double Q1 FY27 (Rs.141.6 crore) and up 98.8% YoY. Operational EBITDA margin was 38.2% and PAT attributable to shareholders rose 50.7% YoY to Rs.89.5 crore. H1 FY27 operational EBITDA margin was 35.1%, which management said is in line with its mid-30s full-year guidance. Working capital cycle stretched to 379 days from 255 days in Q1, and H1 operating cash flow was negative, which management attributed to back-ended receivables and supplier advances. Management stated that the company remains debt-free with about Rs.968 crore of cash and bank balances.

segments.name: Advanced defence simulators (ADS)/Simulators
segments.commentary: Management said simulators typically carry higher margins than ADS; FY26's 48% margin reflected a simulator-heavy mix. Around Rs.400 crore of simulator orders are expected, though timing is uncertain. Naval combat training nodes built from ARI and Anawave acquisitions are at pipeline stage with no order yet.

segments.name: Counter-drone (C-UAS)
segments.commentary: No C-UAS orders have been placed as tenders are yet to float. Management expects FTP-linked orders in Q4 FY27 at the earliest, with possible spillover to Q1 or Q2 FY28. Q2 warranty provisions rose Rs.9.3 crore on higher ADS mix.

segments.name: Hyper Strike interceptor
segments.commentary: Product is in internal trials with no current order book. Capacity being built is about 15,000 units/month on three shifts (180,000 units/year at full ramp), with an initial ramp of about 600 units/month. Revenue expected from FY28, majority of orders in FY29; management assumes an average price of about $10,000 per unit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue now guided at Rs.1,200-1,300 crore; management said it is comfortable achieving 'a little more than' this, with Rs.485 crore already done in H1, implying Rs.715-815 crore in H2.
Full-year operational EBITDA margin guided in the mid-30s; long-term margin guidance of about 35%, varying with ADS/simulator mix.
Management declined to reaffirm the earlier Rs.4,000 crore two-year revenue target or the Rs.2,500-3,000 crore year-end order book scenario, stating the timing of government orders is uncertain.
Capex budgeted at around Rs.150 crore each for FY27 and FY28.
R&D spend expected to stay near FY26 level of about 12% of revenue; no internal R&D target set.

Management expects orders from exports (Middle East, CIS, Southeast Asia) in the next few months, a US prime collaboration likely next year, and Europe (SAFE programme) developments by early next year.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex budgeted at around Rs.150 crore; FY28 capex budgeted at a similar amount.
Hyper Strike capacity of about 15,000 units/month on three shifts; 180,000 units/year at full ramp; initial plan of about 600 units/month.
Patent portfolio: more than 235 patents filed; grants now being announced in consolidated form rather than monthly press releases.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of Rs.481.8 crore in Q2 exceeded the Rs.345.1 crore executed, lifting the order book from Rs.1,239 crore to Rs.1,375.7 crore.
Management said FTP (Fast Track Procurement) approvals have been granted and RFPs are expected within weeks to months; FTP deadline is 31 March 2027, with possible spillover to Q1 or Q2 FY28.
C-UAS addressable share estimated at 70-80% of the market; management does not bid for very low-end systems. Management said capital acquisition orders could take two to three years.
Middle East counter-drone interest exists but no advanced-stage orders; Europe SAFE programme requires 65% local content.
Warranty provisions increased on higher ADS mix; employee and other expenses were 24.4% of revenue vs 26.3% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of Rs.1,200-1,300 crore still valid, given the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to achieve a little more than Rs.1,200-1,300 crore, with Rs.485 crore already executed in H1 and the rest to be executed over Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.2,500-3,000 crore order book by March 2027 and the Rs.4,000 crore two-year target still in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not sure of the Rs.2,500-3,000 crore order book; it would only guide more precisely closer to Q4 and said it is not putting a number on new orders.

qa_highlights.question: Which orders could come in if FTPs slip 6-9 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mainly counter-drone systems, plus about Rs.400 crore of simulator orders, which are taking time to materialise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on Hyper Strike and when is revenue expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Product is in internal trials with no current order; significant contribution is expected by next year (FY28), with majority of orders in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any deferment or delay risk in executing the current order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not foresee any deferment or delays in executing existing orders; the Q1-to-Q2 slippage was a one-time spillover.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.1,375.7 crore order book flagged to convert within six months, and how do the naval acquisitions fit?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Rs.485 crore is already done and the remainder is to be executed over the next two quarters; management described naval CTNs (ARI and Anawave) as a pipeline with no order yet.

risks_watch: Timing of FTP and C-UAS tender floats; management said orders may spill into FY28 and cannot give a firm date.
Working capital cycle at 379 days and negative H1 operating cash flow; receivables and inventory need to convert to cash.
Margin mix sensitivity: management said simulators carry higher margins; warranty provisions rise with ADS mix.
Export and US/Europe market entry remain unquantified; management indicated next-year timelines.
Rising R&D and acquisition-led expansion, including the Cogknit acquisition, which management said may contribute significantly only in about five years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and near-term revenue, but evasive on order timing and FY28 numbers; management repeatedly declined to reaffirm the Rs.2,500-3,000 crore order-book and Rs.4,000 crore two-year targets, citing government procurement delays.
